suitability,essentiality andvitalityofthesub-project.Thissite
is not only selected for economic,social valuebut also for
global environmental climate change mitigations options in
reducing global weather patterns on broad perspectives.This
CommitteerequestedtoDivisionalForestOfficertake
necessary stepforplanting.
16Species When thebestpossibleinformation hasbeen collected onthe
selection characteristicsof the site tobeplanted,thenext stepis the
selection of thetree species toplant.The aim is tochoose
species which are suited to the site,will remain healthy
throughout the anticipated rotation,will produce acceptable
growth and yield,and will meet the objectives of the
plantation (fuel wood production, protection, etc).
17 Timeof The planting season (June) generally coincides with the rainy
planting season;usually,planting is started as soon as a specified
quantity of rain hasfallen.This amount ofprecipitationmust
be judged on thebasis of local knowledge.Planting can also
beinitiated when thesoil is wet to a specified depth
(approximately20 centimeters).

21 Climate The climateofNoakhali islargelytropicaland humid.
Condition Noakhali isknown asacoastal.district while the climate
variations are often hazardous and devastating.Naturally,the
maximum rainfall occurs andnumber ofrainy days occursin
July and August （698.7mm.On the other hand,highest
rainfall occurs 2691 mm in monsoon (June, July,August and
September).After the post monsoon (October and
November), the rainfall drops down to average 1459 mm. In
addition,the temperature of Noakhali ismildpattern.Mayis
the hottest temperature up to 31.9°C and January is the
lowest temperatureup to14.9°C.
22  Planting Theplantation site is a rural plain Canal Dams. On the month
method of June,both sidesof the Canal Dams bushes have been
cleaned tomake suitable for theplantation.On the same
month,Arharhas alsobeengivenwith aview to support the
seedlings by making line. On the following month,pits have
beendonewith the sizeof 30cmx30cmx30cmkeeping
distance inbetween pits2m.Moreover,mixed Cow dung and
ChemicalFertilizerputinto thepitsaccording to theSUFAL
ProjectManual'slandpreparationfor theplantation.For
raising strip plantation,10,000 (Ten thousand) matured
seedlings of several species such as Jhaw,Amlaki,Horitaki,
Bohera, Mango, Kalojam, Gouva, Akashmoni, Arjun,
Mehogony,Chikrashi,Kishnachura,Bokain,Gamar,Amra,
Jack Fruits, Neem, Panial, EpilEpil,Kat Badam,Hijol,
Sonduri etc.havebeenplantedinthenourished/preparedpits.
Afterthat,5fitsizesticksputinthesoilwhicharetiedbythe
rope with the seedlings. Since,there are the chances of
grazing and other unavoidable harmful activities,a number of
Watchershavebeen appointed to tackle theplantation site
fromdamage and deterioration.Besides,selected
beneficiariesandfieldlevelstaffoftheForestDepartmentare
alsolookingaftertheplantationsite.AnAgreementbetween
theForestDepartmentactingonbehalfofTheGovernmentof
thePeople's Republicof Bangladesh (1sParty)and Land

Selected Beneficiaries （Third Party)is or will be done.
Furthermore,a Forest management committee will also be
formedwithintheplantationsitefromtheselected

Km StripPlantation.

B. Characteristic of the Plantation Site
1 Area of the plantation 400.0 ha. Mangrove Plantation at Char Kalam & New Char
Yunus the year of 2020-2021.
2 Edaphic Condition Physiographically the char is part of the young Meghna
EstuarineFlood plain.The site(CharKalam & New Char
Yunus)is muddy softand soft banks of small creek as well
as canal. these soilspermit easyPenetration of Nypa
Fruticans (Kere tree roots because of being quite fertile.
3 Climate Condition The yolaf Char has a monsoon Climate. Characterized by
basically four seasons per year. The average temperature
      s 
C during summer. The average annual rainfalls is 3257
mm and variesfrom 2500 mm to 4500mm.Cyclones
pass regularly, particularly at the beginning and at the end
of the monsoon.The Char is slightly raised flat land which
generally inundates twice a day noticeably from March to
December. The rate of silt deposition is higher
particularly from November to February roughly 3"-4".

4 Brief History MangroveplantationsiteatCharKalam&NewChar
Yunus is muddy and soft banks of small creeks and
canals.The site is the banks of canals that drain water
from the central depression of a char.Generally 2 months
old seedlings should be taken out of the nursery and
planted in the field to minimize root injury. They have
been planted at 1.5 mx 1.5m spacing. The site is not
subjected to heavy siltation or prone to heavy erosion,
while raising keora plantations. In planting Keora/Gewa
strong 1 ft stake has been used against each seedlings
planted. Since keora/Gewa plantations are planted in
lines; the funding may be based on "hectare", planting of
4444 seedlings have been taken as “one seedling hectare."
5 SelectionCriteriaof The plantation site has been selected through the
the Planting Site following criteria:
Land suitability: keore plantation site is muddy and
some uri grasshasgrow&it would beveryhelpful
for hard the soil for a established char formation
the plantation site is stand allover char.
GrazingProblem:Itisknowntothatthereentire
are a number of chars in Noakhali and accreting
new lands. These chars are threat to the grazing
problems.Butthisisfreefromsuchunavoidable
phenomenon.That iswhythissiteusselectedfor
the mangrove plantation.
Biodiversity Conservation: The Coastal
afforestation program will bring a result in the
establishment of plantation rich in biodiversity and
higher density of wildlife habitats. Natural
regenerationofforesttreespecieswiththeir
associates will be enhanced. In addition, through
the project area the condition of coastal forest in
Bangladeshwill extent.
Sectoral Target: The people residing in the project
area are exposed to frequent cyclones and tidal
surge which makes them highly vulnerable to
recent climate effects.As a result,their socio-
economic condition is less secured. Beside this, the
land mass developed due toaccretionof the
sedimentsdischargedthrough hMeghnaestuary
needs to be stabilized. On the other hand ，the
objectivesof theforestrysector istoincrease the
totalforest cover of the countryand tooptimize
sustainable production of goods and services from
the existing limited forest resources. The coastal

area of the proposed project is such type of land
where forestry resources could be developed
throughestablishmentofplantations.
National Strategy: The proposed project is also
aligned with the national strategy; According to the
plan,existingscattered coastal areaswill beplanted
to increase productivity by promoting scientific
management principles. In order to prevent the
extent of damage by cyclones and tidal surges, the
plan envisages creating a Coastal Green Belt and
enhancing access tom input materials, including
‘ seeds and seedlings. In addition, past climate
disasters have shown that resilience to cyclones and
storm surges is grater where mangrove greenbelts
and buffer ecosystems exist. It is evident that
mangroves can mitigate or reduce risk of natural
disasters such as cyclones and tsunamis.
GlobalAspect:AccordingtotheIPCCreportof
2013, approximately 95% human beings are
responsiblefortheclimatechange andBangladesh
is the home to the world's largest delta systems.
Two third of the country is less than five meters
above the sealevel.It is vulnerable to short term
climate shocks such as cyclone (DFID-2011) while
the country is among top ten countries which are to
climate change (Maple Craft-2013). As a result,
human beings and natural resources are threats to
climate change. So, there is no alternative without
afforestation andreforestationinthecoastalzones.
That iswhyChar Kalam&NewChar Yunus is
selected for raisingKeora/Gewaplantation.
6 ClimateResilient Through the afforestation in the project area biodiversity
Aspect of the conservation,human security and so on will be ensured in
Plantation the project area. Therefore, greenbelt of the project area
by raising said plantation has been planned to bring back
the balance of eco-system into the same char lands and to
developafriendly /environmentbyraisingcoastal
afforestation.Itisforthefactthatthelandissuitablefor
mangrove and non-mangrove plantations where bio-
physical and socio-economic conditions will  improve.
The Char Kalam & New Char Yunus will be brought to
work asabarrierduringnaturaldisastersbydintof the
raised plantation.
C OtherActivities

Delineation of the The Char Kalam & New Char Yunus is a newly formed
Planting Area char land which has raised rapidly. The char is adjacent to
the East-North side of Keora/Gewa plantation. The soils
of the site
Permiteasypenetration ofkeoratreerootsbecause of
being fertile. Theproject site would be used for different
types of species diversity plantation. If the coastal forest
lands of a target area are properly replenished with
greens, the existing wildlife habitats will increase and will
be a nice environment for biodiversity conservation.This
type of coastal forest lands can fight back the prevailing
environmental threats and mitigate the negative impacts
of the climate change took place in these coastal zones.
Thus,this type of coastal forest lands not only save the
life and resources from natural disasters but also play
important role in economic development.

2 subjected to more saline condition.These soils permit easy

four seasons per year. The average temperature usually ranges
3 The average annual rainfall is3257 mm (Islam2009) andvariesfrom
2500 mm to 4500mm.Cyclonespass regularly,particularly at the

Selection Criteriaof Theplantationsitehasbeenselected throughthefollowingcriteria.
the Planting Site a.Land suitability:The landof the planting site(New Jaliar Char
and Khager char) is soft and clayey.In addition,the site is
comparativelycompactand harderaswell asat the same time

subject to more saline condition where Mangrove seedlings e.g.
Keora(Sonneratiaapetala) ue Excoecaria agallocha
(Gewa)are suitableforplantation.
b. GrazingProblem:Itisknown to that there entire areanumberof

plantation.
Biodiversity Conservation:The Coastal afforestation program will
bring a resultin theestablishmentofplantationrichinbiodiversity
andhigher density ofwildlifehabitats.Natural regenerationof
forest tree species with their associates will be enhanced.In
addition,through theproject area the conditionofcoastal forest in
Bangladesh will extent.
d. Poverty Reduction:The project activities are comprised of civil
works,nursery and plantation raising and maintenance,gardening
etc.;which are labour intensive and technical works.Male and
female canbe deployed or engaged inall theseworks based on
theirworking capability;whichwillcreateemployment
opportunitiesforthemandhelptheminalleviatingpovertyand
fulfillingneeds.Thus theywill bebenefited socio-economically
and theirsocial esteemwillbe elevated.
e. Sectoral Target: The people residing in the project area are
exposed to frequentcyclones and tidal surge which makes them
highly vulnerable to recent climate change effects.As a result,
their socio-economic condition is less secured.Beside this, the
landmassdevelopeddue to accretionof thesedimentsdischarged
through Meghna estuary needs tobe stabilized.On theother
hand,the objectives of the forestry sector is to increase the total
forestcoverof the country and to optimize sustainableproduction
ofgoods andservicesfromtheexistinglimitedforestresources.
The coastal area of the proposed project is such type of landwhere
forestryresources couldbe developed through establishment of
plantations.
f.
National Strategy;theBangladeshSixthFiveYearPlan(FY2023-
FY2024).According to the plan,existing scattered coastal areas
will be planted toincrease productivity by promoting scientific
management principles.In order to prevent the extentof damage
by cyclones and tidal surges,the plan envisages creating a Coastal
Green Belt and enhancing access to input materials,including
seeds andseedlings.In addition,past climate disastershave shown
that resilience to cyclones and storm surges is greater where
mangrove greenbelts and buffer ecosystems exist.It is evident that
mangroves canmitigate orreduceriskofnatural disasterssuch as
cyclonesandtsunamis.
g. Global Aspect:According to theIPCC reportof 2013,
approximately95%human beings are theresponsiblefor the

climate shocks such as cyclone (DFID-2011). As a result,

humanbeingsand naturalresources are threats toclimate
change.So,there is no alternative without afforestation and
reforestation in the coastal zones.That is why“NewJaliar Char
andKhagerchar”isselected formangrove plantation.
5 ClimateResilient ★ The Coastal forest,breakwater,seawall is to absorb the impact
Aspectofthe forces and to retard theflow of large stormwaves and cyclone.A
Plantation seawall,if tall enough,reflects the waves back out to sea.On the
other hand,permeable structures,like breakwaters and coastal
forests,partlyreflectandpartly transmit thewater.In thecaseofa
coastal forest, energy is progressively absorbed as it passes
through theforest.Withouttheforestbarrier,the tsunami/cyclone
willrun-up to amaximumheightdetermined by themagnitude
andnatureoftheseismic event thatcreatedthe tsunami andlocal
factors such as the coastal profile,offshore bathymetry and beach
slope thatmodify thewave'sforce.Once the tsunami comeson
shore,theamountofreductioninwaterdepth,velocity,andforce
dependsonhowmuch waterisreflected and energy is absorbed
bythecoastalforest.

Selection Criteria of Theplantation site hasbeen selected through the followingcriteria.
the Planting Site a. Land suitability:The land of the planting site (New Char Nur

Islam) is sof and clayey.In addition,the site is comparatively

Grazing Problem:It is known to that there entire are a number of

plantation
Biodiversity Conservation:The Coastal afforestation program will
bring aresult in the establishment ofplantationrich inbiodiversity
and higher density of wildlife habitats.Natural regeneration of
forest tree species with their associates will be enhanced. In
addition,through the project area the condition of coastal forest in
Bangladesh will extent.
P Poverty Reduction:The project activities are comprised of civil
works,nursery and plantation raising and maintenance,gardening
etc.;which are labor intensive and technical works. Male and
female can be deployed or engaged in all these works based on
their working capability;which will Icreateemployment
opportunities for them and help them in alleviating poverty and
fulfilling needs. Thus they will be benefited socio-economically
and their social esteem will beelevated
Sectoral Target:The people residing in the project area are
highly vulnerable to recent climate change effects. As a result,
their socio-economic condition is less secured. Beside this,the
land mass developed due to accretion of the sediments discharged
through Meghna estuary needs to be stabilized.On the other
hand, the objectives of the forestry sector is to increase the total
forest cover of the country and to optimize sustainable production
of goods and services from the existing limited forest resources.
The coastal area of the proposed project is such type of land where
forestry resources could be developed through establishment of
plantations.
National Strategy:The proposed project is also aligned with the
National Strategy,the Bangladesh Sixth Five Year Plan (FY2019-
FY2023).According to the plan,existing scattered coastal areas
will be planted to increase productivity by promoting scientific
management principles. In order to prevent the extent of damage
by cyclones and tidal surges, the plan envisages creating a Coastal
Green Belt and enhancing access to input materials, including
seeds and seedlings.In addition,past climate disasters have shown
that resilience to cyclones and storm surges is greater where
mangrove greenbelts and buffer ecosystems exist. It is evident that
mangroves can mitigate or reduce risk ofnatural disasters such as
cyclones and tsunamis.
g. Global Aspect:According to the IPCC report of 2013,
approximately95%humanbeings are theresponsible for the
climate change and Bangladesh is the home to the world’s
largest delta systems. Two third of the country is less than

five meters above the sea level. It isvulnerable to short term
climate shocks such as cyclone （DFID-20ll). As a result,
human beings and natural resources are threats to climate
change. So,there is no alternative without afforestation and
reforestation in the coastal zones. That is why “New Char Nur
Islam"is selected for mangrove plantation.
5 Climate Resilient The Coastal forest, breakwater, seawall is to absorb the impact
Aspect of the forces and to retard the flow of large storm waves and cyclone.A
Plantation seawall,if tall enough,reflects the waves back out to sea.On the
other hand,permeable structures,like breakwaters and coastal
forests,partly reflect and partly transmit the water.In the case of a
coastal forest, energy is progressively absorbed as it passes
through the forest.Without the forest barrier,the tsunami/cyclone
willrun-up to a maximum height determined by the magnitude
and natureof the seismic event thatcreated the tsunami and local
factors such as the coastal profile,offshore bathymetry and beach
slope that modify thewave's force.Once the tsunami comes on
shore,the amount ofreduction in water depth,velocity,and force
depends on how much water is reflected and energy is absorbed
by thecoastal forest.
Through the afforestation in the project area biodiversity
conservation,human security and so on will be ensured in the
project area.Therefore,greenbelt of the project area by rising said
plantation has been planned to bring back the balance of eco-
system into the same char lands and to develop a friendly
environment by raising coastal afforestation.It is for the fact that
the land is suitable for mangrove and non-mangrove plantations
where bio-physical and socio-economic conditions will improve.
The New Char Nur Islam will be brought to work asa barrier
during natural disasters by dint of the mangrove plantation.

Biodiversity Conservation:The Coastal afforestation program will
bring a result in the establishment of plantation rich inbiodiversity
and higher density of wildlife habitats. Natural regeneration of
forest tree species with their associates will be enhanced. In
addition,through the project area the condition of coastal forest in
Bangladesh will extent.
Poverty Reduction:The project activities are comprised of civil
works,nursery and plantation raising and maintenance,gardening

their working capability,which will create employment
opportunities for them and help them in alleviating poverty and
fulfilling needs.Thus they will be benefited socio-economically
and their social esteem will be elevated.
Sectoral Target: The people residing in the project area are
exposed to frequent cyclones and tidal surge which makes them
highly vulnerable to recent climate change effects.As a result
their socio-economic condition is less secured.Beside this,the
land mass developed due to accretion of the sediments discharged
through Meghna estuary needs to be stabilized. On the other
hand,the objectives of the forestry sector is to increase the total
forest cover of the country and to optimize sustainable production
ofgoods and services from the existinglimited forest resources.

forestry resources could be developed through establishment of
plantations.

National Strategy,the Bangladesh Sixth FiveYear Plan (FY2020-
FY2024). According to the plan, existing scattered coastal areas

management principles. In order to prevent the extent of damage
by cyclones and tidal surges,the plan envisages creating a Coastal

Selection Criteria of The plantation site has been selected through the following criteria.
the Planting Site a.Land suitability:The land of the planting site (New Char Achia
and New Jaliar Char) is soft and clayey.In addition, the site is
comparatively compact and harder aswell as at the same time

subject to more saline condition where Mangrove seedlings e.g.
Keora （Sonneratiaapetala)and Excoecaria agallocha
(Gewa)are suitable for plantation.
b. GrazingProblem:It is known to that thereentire are a number of
chars in Noakhali and accreting new lands. These chars are threat
to the grazing problems.But this is free from such unavoidable
phenomenon. That is why this site is selected for the mangrove
plantation.
Biodiversity Conservation:The Coastal afforestation program will
bring aresult in the establishment ofplantation rich inbiodiversity
and higher density of wildlife habitats.Natural regeneration of
forest tree species with their associates will be enhanced. In
addition,through the project area the condition of coastal forest in
Bangladeshwill extent.
'P Poverty Reduction:The project activities are comprised of civil
works,nursery and plantation raising and maintenance,gardening
etc. which are labor intensive and technical works. Male and
female can be deployed or engaged in all these works based on
their working capability;which will create employment
opportunities for them and help them in alleviating poverty and
fulfilling needs. Thus they will be benefited socio-economically
and their social esteem will beelevated.
Sectoral Target: The people residing in the project area are
exposed to frequent cyclones and tidal surge which makes them
highly vulnerable to recent climate change effects. As a result,
their socio-economic condition is less secured. Beside this, the
landmass developed due to accretion of the sediments discharged
through Meghna estuary needs to be stabilized.On the other
hand,the objectives of the forestry sector is to increase the total
forest cover of the country and to optimize sustainableproduction
of goods and services from the existing limited forest resources.
The coastal area of the proposed project is such type of landwhere
forestry resources could be developed through establishment of
plantations.
f National Strategy: The proposed project is also aligned with the
National Strategy;theBangladeshSixthFive YearPlan(FY2022-
FY2023).According to the plan,existing scattered coastal areas
will be planted to increase productivity by promoting scientific
management principles.In order to prevent the extent of damage
by cyclones and tidal surges,the plan envisages creating a Coastal
Green Belt and enhancing access to input materials, including
seeds and seedlings.In addition,past climate disasters have shown
that resilience to cyclones and storm surges is greater where
mangrovegreenbelts andbuffer ecosystems exist.It is evident that
mangroves can mitigate or reduce risk ofnatural disasters such as
cyclonesand tsunamis
Global Aspect:According to the IPCC report of 2013,
approximately95%human beings are theresponsible for the
climate change and Bangladesh is the home to the world's
largestdelta systems.Two third ofthe country is less than
five meters above the sea level.It is vulnerable to short term
climate shocks such as cyclone (DFID-2011). As a result

human beings and natural resources are threats to climate
change.So,there is no alternative without afforestation and
reforestation in the coastal zones.That is why “New Char Achia
and NewJaliar Char”is selected formangrove plantation.
5 Climate Resilient ★ The Coastal forest,breakwater,seawall is to absorb the impact
Aspect ofthe forces and to retard the flow of large storm waves and cyclone.A
Plantation seawall,if tall enough,reflects the waves back out to sea.On the
other hand,permeable structures,like breakwaters and coastal
forests,partly reflect and partly transmit the water.In the case ofa
coastal forest, energy is progressively absorbed as it passes
through the forest.Without theforest barrier,the tsunami/cyclone
will run-up to a maximum height determined by the magnitude
andnatureofthe seismicevent thatcreated the tsunami and local
factors such as the coastal profile,offshore bathymetry and beach
slope that modify the wave's force.Once the tsunami comes on
shore,theamountofreduction inwater depth,velocity,and force
depends on how much water is reflected and energy is absorbed
by thecoastalforest.
Through the afforestation in the project area biodiversity
conservation,human security and so on will be ensured in the
project area.Therefore,greenbeltof theproject area byrising said
plantation has been planned to bring back the balance of eco-
system into the same char lands and to develop a friendly
environment by raising coastal afforestation.It is for the fact that
the land is suitable for mangrove and non-mangrove plantations
where bio-physical and socio-economic conditions will improve.
TheNew CharAchia and NewJaliar Charwill be brought to work
as a barrier during natural disasters by dint of the mangrove
plantation.

3 The average annual rainfall is3257 mm(Islam 2009) and variesfrom

Selection Criteria of Theplantation site hasbeenselected through the following criteria.
the Planting Site a. Land suitability:The land of theplanting site (New Jahajir Char)
is soft and clayey.In addition, the site is comparatively compact
and harder as well as at the same time subject to more saline
condition where Mangrove seedlings e.g. Keora (Sonneratia
apetala) and Excoecaria agallocha （Gewa)are suitable for
plantation.

b. GrazingProblem:It is known to that there entire are a number of
chars in Noakhali and accreting new lands. These chars are threat
to the grazing problems.But this is free from such unavoidable
phenomenon.That is why this site is selected for the mangrove
plantation.
Biodiversity Conservation:The Coastal afforestation program will
bring a result in the establishment ofplantation rich in biodiversity
and higher density of wildlife habitats.Natural regeneration of
forest tree species with their associates will be enhanced.In
addition,through theproject area the condition of coastal forest in
Bangladesh will extent.
Poverty Reduction:The project activities are comprised of civil
works,nursery and plantation raising and maintenance,gardening
etc.:which are labor intensive and technical works.Male and
female can be deployed or engaged in all these works based on
their working capability; which will create employment
opportunities for them and help them in alleviating poverty and
fulfilling needs. Thus, they will be benefited socio-economically
and their social esteem will be elevated.
e. Sectoral Target:The people residing in the project area are
exposed to frequent cyclones and tidal surge which makes them
highly vulnerable to recent climate change effects. As a result,
their socio-economic condition is less secured. Beside this,the
land mass developed due to accretion of the sediments discharged
through Meghna estuary needs to be stabilized.On the other
hand, the objectives of the forestry sector are to increase the total
forestcover of the country and to optimize sustainableproduction
ofgoods and services from the existing limited forest resources.
The coastal area of theproposed project is such type of landwhere
forestry resources could be developed through establishment of
plantations.
f National Strategy:The proposed project is also aligned with the
National Strategy;the Bangladesh SixthFive YearPlan FY2020-
FY2024).According to the plan,existing scattered coastal areas
will be planted to increaseproductivity by promoting scientific
management principles.In order to prevent the extent of damage
by cyclones and tidal surges,the plan envisages creatinga Coastal
Green Belt and enhancing access to input materials, including
seeds and seedlings.In addition,past climate disasters have shown
that resilience to cyclones and storm surges is greater where
mangrove greenbelts and buffer ecosystems exist.It is evident that
mangroves can mitigate or reduce risk of natural disasters such as
cyclonesandtsunamis.
g. Global Aspect: According to the IPCC report of 2013,
approximately 95% human beings are the responsible for the
climate change and Bangladesh is the home to theworld's largest
delta systems. Two third of the country is less than five meters
above the sea level.It isvulnerable to short term climate shocks
such as cyclone (DFID-2011). As a result, human beings and
natural resources are threats to climate change. So,there is no
alternative without afforestation and reforestation in the coastal
zones. That is why “New Jahajjir Char”is selected for mangrove
plantation.

Aspect of the forces and to retard the flow of large storm waves and cyclone.A

Plantation seawall,if tall enough,reflects the waves back out to sea.On the
other hand,permeable structures,like breakwaters and coastal
forests,partly reflect and partly transmit the water.In the case ofa
coastal forest, energy is progressively absorbed as it passes
through the forest.Without the forest barrier,the tsunami/cyclone
willrun-up to a maximum height determined by the magnitude
and nature of the seismic event that created the tsunami and local
factors such as the coastalprofile,offshore bathymetry and beach
slope that modify the wave’s force.Once the tsunami comes on
shore,theamountofreductioninwater depth,velocity,andforce
depends on how much water is reflected and energy is absorbed
by thecoastal forest.

13.Site Selection Criteria The plantation site is selected through the meeting with
UP Chairman, UP Members and other local Elites. In that
meeting BFD Officials inform to the attendees about the
suitability, essentiality and vitality of the sub-project. This
site is not only selected for economic, social value but also
forglobal environmental climatechangemitigations options
in reducing global weather patterns on broad perspectives.

14.Species selection When the best possible information has been collected
on the characteristics of the site to be planted, the next step is
the selection of the tree species to plant. The aim is to choose
species which are suited to the site, will remain healthy
throughout the anticipated rotation, will produce acceptable
growthandyield, andwill meet the objectives of the
plantation (fuel wood production, protection, etc.).
15. Time of planting The planting season (June) generally coincides with the
Rainy season; usually, planting is started as soon as a
specifiedquantityof rainhasfallen.This amount of
precipitation must be judged on the basis of local knowledge.
Planting can also be initiated when the soil is wet to a
specified depth (approximately 20 centimeters).
16.Edaphic Condition The plantation site is a rustic/pastoral/rural. Soils are
mainly grey to olive, deep, silt loams. Organic matter.
contents are medium Newly constructed road by Union
Parishad.
17. Topography Slopesonbothsidesoftheroadwhererainwaterdoes
not accumulate and there is no difficulty in moving vehicles
along the road which is suitable for planting.
18.Soil structure ° Sandy loam soil
19. Climate Condition The climate of Noakhali is largely tropical and humid.
Noakhaliisknownasacoastaldistrictwhiletheclimate
variations are often hazardous and devastating. Naturally, the
maximumrainfall occurs and number ofrainydays occursin
July and August (698.7 mm. On the other hand, highest
rainfall occurs 2691 mm in monsoon (June, July, August and
September). After the post monsoon (October and
November), the rainfall drops down to average 1459 mm. In
addition, the temperature of Noakhali is mild pattern. May is
the hottest temperature upto 31.9 ° C and January is the
lowest temperature up to 14.9 ° C.
20.Planting method ° Theplantationsite is a rural plain road and it is
connected to themainroad.Theroad isfamousforthename
of(a) 2 no.CharParbuti Union From Maharun NeasSchool

Companigonj, Noakhali. The road is surrounded with arable/

seen/existed. On the month of June, both sides of the road's
busheshavebeen cleaned tomake suitablefor the plantation.
On the same month,Arharhas alsobeengivenwith a viewto
support the

seedlings by making line at both sides of the road. On the
following month, pits have been done with the size of 30cm
x30cmx30cm keeping distance in between pits 2m.
Moreover,mixed Cowdungand Chemical Fertilizerputinto
the pits according to the SUFAL Manual's land preparation
for the plantation. For raising strip plantation, 100oo (Ten
thousand) matured seedlings of several species such as Jhaw,
Raintree, Akashmoni, Mehogoni, Menjiam, Neem, Arjun,
Guava, Amloki, Tetul, Jackfruit, Jam, Khejur, Boroi, Babla,
Natai, Ipil-ipil, Shisu, Gamar, Koronja etc. have been planted
in the nourished/ prepared pits. After that, 5 fit size sticks put
in the soil which are tied by the rope with the seedlings.
Since, there are the chances of grazing and other unavoidable
harmful activities, a number of Watchers have been appointed
to tackle the plantation site from damage and deterioration.
Besides,selected beneficiaries and field level staff of the
Forest Department are also looking after the plantation site.
An Agreement between the Forest Department acting on
behalf of The Government of the People's Republic of
Bangladesh (1"t Party) and Land Owing Agencies (2"d Party)
and Group of Local Participants-Selected Beneficiaries (Third
Party) is or will be done. Furthermore, a committee will also
be formed within the plantation site from the selected
beneficiaries to make sustainable of the ongoing 12 Seedling

13. Species selection When the best possible information has been collected
on the characteristics of the site tobe planted,the next
step is the selection of the tree species to plant. The aim
is to choose species which are suited to the site,will
remain healthy throughout the anticipated rotation, will
produce acceptable growth and yield, and will meet the
objectives of the plantation (fuel wood production,
protection, etc.).
14. Time of planting The planting season (June) generally coincides with the
Rainy season; usually, planting is started as soon as a
specified quantity of rain has fallen. This amount of
precipitation must be judged on the basis of local
knowledge. Planting can also be initiated when the soil
is wet to aspecified depth(approximately20
centimeters).

15.Edaphic Condition The plantation site is a rustic/pastoral/rural. Soils are
mainly grey to olive, deep, silt loams. Organic matter.
contents are medium Newly constructed road by Union
Parishad.
16. Topography Slopesonbothsidesoftheroadwhererainwaterdoes
not accumulate and there is no difficulty in moving
vehicles along the road which is suitable for planting.
17.Soil structure Sandy loam soil
18.ClimateCondition The climateof Noakhali is largely tropical and humid.
Noakhali is known as a coastal district while the climate
variations are often hazardous anddevastating.
Naturally,the maximum rainfall occurs and number of
rainy days occurs in July and August (698.7 mm. On
the other hand, highest rainfall occurs 2691 mm in
monsoon (June, July, August and September). After the
post monsoon (October and November), the rainfall
drops down to average 1459 mm. In addition, the
temperatureof Noakhali ismildpattern.Mayisthe
hottest temperature upto 31.9 ° C and January is the
lowest temperature up to 14.9 ° C.
19. Planting method The plantationsiteisaruralplainroadofNew
Embankment and it is connected to the Old
Embankment.The road is famous for the name of
Muktaria ghat, Hatiya, Noakhali. The road is
surrounded with arable/ agricultural,humansettlements
while scattered trees are seen/existed. On the month of
June, both sides of the road's bushes have been cleaned
to make suitable for the plantation. On the same month,
Arhar has also been given with a view to support the
seedlings by making line at both sides of the road. On
the following month, pits have been done with the size
of30cmx30cmx30cmkeepingdistanceinbetweenpits
2m. Moreover, mixed Cowdung andChemical
Fertilizer put into the pits according to the SUFAL
Manual's land preparation for the plantation. For
raising strip plantation, 5000 (Five thousand) matured
seedlings of several species such as Jhaw, Akashmoni,
Sundari, Pashur, Guava, Jambura, Amloki, Jalpai,
Raintree, Lambu.etc. have been planted in the
nourished/prepared pits.After that, 5 fit size sticks put
in the soil which are tied by the rope with the seedlings.
Since,there are the chances of grazing and other
unavoidableharmfulactivities,anumberofWatchers
have been appointed to tackle the plantation site from
damage and deterioration. Besides, S selected
beneficiariesandfieldlevelstaffoftheForest
Department are also looking after the plantation site. An

behalfofTheGovernmentofthePeople'sRepublicof

Party) and   Groupof   Local Participants-Selected
Beneficiaries (Third Party) is or will be done.

the plantation site from the selected beneficiaries to
make sustainable of the ongoing 12 Seedling Km Strip

The people of Bangladesh, a densely populated country, depend heavily on forests for fuel wood,
timber and other subsistence. Due to huge biotic and abiotic pressure, forest resources of the
country have been depleted greatly. Participatory social forestry was introduced in Bangladesh in
early 1980s to reduce the rampant rate of deforestation. Social forestry, involving local people in
a benefit-sharing mechanism, has been introduced to Bangladesh as a remedy to stop rampant
deforestation. This added income is a significant contribution to local monetary resources and
improves the socioeconomic conditions of the poor.It is found that individuals recognized as
encroachers in the past, have now become vital stakeholders of forests and recognized member in
community The application of social forestry practices to strip plantations in Bangladesh could
be a key factor in significantly reducing poverty and could also stem the rising tide of forest
resource losses.

The people of Bangladesh, a densely populated country, depend heavily on forests for fuel wood,
timber and other subsistence. Due to huge biotic and abiotic pressure, forest resources of the
country have been depleted greatly. Participatory social forestry was introduced in Bangladesh in
early 1980s to reduce the rampant rate of deforestation. Social forestry, involving local people in
a benefit-sharing mechanism, has been introduced to Bangladesh as a remedy to stop rampant
deforestation. This added income is a significant contribution to local monetary resources and
improves the socioeconomic conditions of the poor. It is found that individuals recognized as
encroachers in the past, have now become vital stakeholders of forests and recognized member in
community The application of social forestry practices to strip plantations in Bangladesh could
be a key factor in significantly reducing poverty and could also stem the rising tide of forest
resource losses.

19 Planting method The plantation site is a rural plain road and it is connected to the
main road. The road is famous for the name of (a) Roads on both
sides adjacent to Malek canal (b) Road adjacent toHanif Bapari
canal (c) Darbash Bazar Mujib Killah Road to Ladu market

canal (g) Factory road & East Char Amanullah Gov. Primary
School RoadviaMosjid Market of CharAmanullah,CharJabbar
, Char Clark & Char Jubelee Union Parishad-Noakhali. The road
is surrounded with arable/ agricultural, human settlements while
scattered trees are seen/existed. On the month of June, both sides
of the road's bushes have been cleaned to make suitable for the
plantation. On the same month,Arhar has alsobeen given with a
viewtosupport the seedlings by makingline atbothsides of the
road. On the following month, pits have been done with the size
of 30cm x30cmx30cm keeping distance in between pits 2m.
Moreover, mixed Cow dung and Chemical Fertilizer put into the
pits according totheSUFAL Manual's landpreparationfor the
plantation. For raising strip plantation, 100000 (One Lac)
matured seedlings of several species such as Jhaw, Gouva
Akashmoni, Arjun, Mehogony, Chikrashi, Kishnachura, Bokain,
Gamar, Jam, Amra, Jack Fruits, Nim, Amloki, Haritoki etc. have
been planted in the nourished/prepared pits.After that, 5 fit size
sticks put in the soil which are tied by the rope with the
seedlings. Since, there are the chances of grazing and other
unavoidable harmful activities, a number of Watchers have been
appointed to  tackle the  plantation  site  from damage and
deterioration.Besides, selected beneficiaries and field level staff
of the Forest Department are also looking after the plantation
site. An Agreement between the Forest Department acting on
behalf of The Government of the People's Republic of
Bangladesh (1st Party) and Land Owing Agencies (2nd Party) and
Group of Local Participants-Selected Beneficiaries (Third Party)
is or will be done. Furthermore, a committee will also be formed
within the plantation site from the selected beneficiaries to make
sustainable of the ongoing 100 Seedling Km Strip Plantation.

The people of Bangladesh, a densely populated country, depend heavily on forests for fuel wood,
timber and other subsistence. Due to huge biotic and abiotic pressure, forest resources of the
country have been depleted greatly. Participatory social forestry was introduced in Bangladesh in
early 1980s to reduce the rampant rate of deforestation. Social forestry, involving local people in
a benefit-sharing mechanism, has been introduced to Bangladesh as a remedy to stop rampant
deforestation. This added income is a significant contribution to local monetary resources and
improves the socioeconomic conditions of the poor. It is found that individuals recognized as
encroachers in the past, have now become vital stakeholders of forests and recognized member in
community The application of social forestry practices to strip plantations in Bangladesh could
be a key factor in significantly reducing poverty and could also stem the rising tide of forest
resource losses.

plantation. On the same month, Arhar has also been given with a
view to support the seedlings by making line at both sides of the
road. On the following month, pits have been done with the size

pits according to the SUFAL Manual's land preparation for the
plantation. For raising strip plantation, 10,000 (Ten thousand)
matured seedlings of several species such as Jhaw, Amlaki,
Horitaki, Bohera, Mango, Kalojam, Gouva, Akashmoni, Arjun,
Mehogony, Chikrashi, Kishnachura, Bokain, Gamar, Amra, Jack
Fruits, Neem etc. have been planted in the nourished/prepared
pits. After that, 5 fit size sticks put in the soil which are tied by
the rope with the seedlings. Since, there are the chances of
grazing and other unavoidable harmful activities, a number of
Watchers have been appointed to tackle the plantation site from
damage and deterioration. Besides, selected beneficiaries and
field level staff of the Forest Department are also looking after
the plantation site. An Agreement between the Forest

21 Climate The climate of Noakhali is largely tropical and humid.
Condition Noakhali is known as a coastal district while the climate
variations are often hazardous and devastating. Naturally,
the maximum rainfall occurs and number of rainy days
occurs in July and August (698.7 mm. On the other hand,
highest rainfall occurs 2691 mm in monsoon June, July,
August and September). After the post monsoon (October
and November), the rainfall drops down to average 1459
mm. In addition, the temperature of Noakhali is mild
pattern.May is the hottest temperature up to 31.9° C and
January is the lowest temperature up to 14.9°C.
22Planting The plantation site is a rural plain Canal Dams. On the
method month of June,both sides of the road’s bushes have been
cleaned to make suitable for the plantation.On the same
month,Arhar has also been given with a view to support
the seedlings by making line at both sides of the Canal
Dams. On the following month, pits have been done with
the size of 30cmx30cmx30cm keeping distance in between
pits 2m. Moreover, mixed Cow dung and Chemical
Fertilizer put into the pits according to the SUFAL
Manual's land preparation for the plantation.For raising
strip plantation,10,000 (Ten thousand) matured seedlings
of several species such asJhaw,Amlaki,Horitaki,Bohera,
Mango,Kalojam,Gouva,Akashmoni,Arjun,Mehogony,
Chikrashi, Kishnachura, Bokain,Gamar, Amra, Jack
Fruits,Neem,Panial,Epil Epil,Kat Badam etc.have been
planted in the nourished/prepared pits.After that,5 fit
size sticks put in the soil which are tied by the rope with
the seedlings. Since, there are the chances of grazing and
other unavoidable harmful activities,a number of
Watchers have been appointed to tackle the plantation site
from damage and deterioration. Besides,selected
beneficiaries and field level staffof the ForestDepartment
are also looking after the plantation site.An Agreement
between the Forest Department acting on behalf of The
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh (1st
Party) and Land Owing Agencies (2nd Party) and Group
of Local Participants-Selected Beneficiaries (Third Party)
is or will be done. Furthermore,a Forest management
committee will also be formed within the plantation site
from the selected beneficiaries to make sustainable of the
ongoing 10 Seedling Km Strip Plantation.
